statement: The two benchmark programs cannot fail today, so they are a printout rather than a safeguard. Their scenario selection is worth keeping; their machinery is not.

measuredFindings.finding: A run reports success while measuring nothing
measuredFindings.evidence: dotnet run --filter *SupervisorBenchmark* -> NU1201 net5.0 incompatible, table row NA, 'executed benchmarks: 0', process exit code 0
measuredFindings.cause: Classes pin RuntimeMoniker.NetCoreApp31, Net50 and Net60; those runtimes are not installed.

measuredFindings.finding: One of the two programs does not build
measuredFindings.cause: The project targets net8.0 and therefore hits two different conditional bands of Directory.Packages.props at once (line 39 gives EF Core SqlServer 9.0.1, line 43 gives DI 8.0.0).
measuredFindings.resolution: Retargeting to net10.0 resolves it by construction; no version guess is needed.

measuredFindings.finding: Neither project is in the solution or in any workflow
measuredFindings.consequence: That is why the build break went unnoticed.

measuredFindings.finding: Benchmarks that do not measure the product
items: ConcurrencyBenchmark measures BCL Dictionary against ConcurrentDictionary and would stay green with the entire bus deleted
MediatorBenchmark compares against MediatR, a third party library rather than a capability
JsonSerializationBenchmark.NewtonsoftJson is the last non test consumer of the removed project
BusOutboxBenchmark uses SQL Server over Windows LocalDB while the referenced SQL transport is PostgreSQL only

measuredFindings.consequence: Without a stored series there is nothing to compare, so a number carries no statement about regression.

alreadyCorrected: The container files of the moved benchmark followed the move and no longer start a broker for a removed capability.
whatIsWorthKeeping: The scenario selection: envelope against object serialization path, middleware pipe cost measured singly and combined, supervisor lifecycle, channel dispatch, mediator throughput.
minimumToBeWorthItsPlace: Abort on zero executed benchmarks instead of exiting green.
One job definition instead of per class runtime pins.
Every benchmark constructs the product type directly, so removing the capability breaks the build instead of silently measuring nothing.
Both projects in the CI build; building is enough, running is not.
openDecision: Whether the benchmarks stay developer tooling on demand, as PO-2026-08-13-04 number 5 keeps them, or become a regression safeguard with a stored baseline. Not decided here.
